info.title: ExtorQ Analyst API
info.description:
Read API over ExtorQ's ClickHouse store. The only analyst mutation is the workflow state of
an alert (`POST /alerts/{alert_id}/state`); an investigation context built on demand for an
analyst is also persisted. Both are audited.

**AI is advisory and read-only here.** Jev triage assessments are written by the ai-worker
and listed by `GET /alerts/{alert_id}/assessments`; the API never calls an AI provider and
AI output never changes an alert.

**Authentication.** Every `/api/v1` call needs `Authorization: Bearer <api service token>`
(held only by the console's Next.js server), `X-ExtorQ-User` and `X-ExtorQ-Role`
(`analyst` | `viewer`). Viewers cannot mutate (403). Mutations write an
`analyst_actions` audit row before the change.

**Data honesty.** Values come from stored telemetry; unknown values are `null`; empty
sources yield empty lists plus explicit flags. All strings are untrusted: render as text.

**Lifecycle.** Assets and collectors carry `lifecycle_state` (`active` | `stale` |
`retired`). Retired assets (no collector reports for them and not observed within the
retirement window, 24 h by default) are never deleted, but the asset list, the overview
rollups and the health collector list leave them out unless `include_retired=true`.

**Caching.** Aggregate GET responses (overview, health, assets, services, rules) are reused
for up to `EXTORQ_API_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` (default 15 s); `X-ExtorQ-Cache: hit|miss|off` and
`X-ExtorQ-Cache-Age` say so, and `generated_at` is the computation time. Analyst mutations
clear the cache.

AIProviderHealth.title: AIProviderHealth
AIProviderHealth.description:
One AI provider/task: configuration as the API process sees it, the state of the
component that actually runs it (the ai-worker for Jev triage) and recent outcomes.

AssessmentListResponse.title: AssessmentListResponse
AssessmentListResponse.description:
Advisory Jev triage assessments of one alert, newest first.

Jev never changes severity, suppresses, closes or counts anything: these records sit
next to the deterministic alert and cite the ``context_input_hash`` they were computed
from.

AssetLifecycleSummary.title: AssetLifecycleSummary
AssetLifecycleSummary.description: Lifecycle of the inventory at request time and what the rollups left out.

CollectorStatus.title: CollectorStatus
CollectorStatus.description: Latest report of one collector (``v_collector_latest``) plus derived staleness.

EventListItem.title: EventListItem
EventListItem.description: Flat projection of a stored event for tables (no ``raw``/``payload``).

HostedService.title: HostedService
HostedService.description:
A service of an ANCESTOR asset with present instances on this asset.

Example: a cluster workload (``k8s_workload`` of ``k8s:<cluster>``) whose Pods and
containers run on the node ``k8s:<cluster>/node/<name>``. Only instances whose
``asset_id`` is this asset are listed, and only services whose asset is an ancestor of
it are accepted (an instance cannot attach itself to another asset's service).

ServiceAuthActivity.title: ServiceAuthActivity
ServiceAuthActivity.description: Authentication events attributed to the service (category ``authentication``).

ServiceEndpointView.title: ServiceEndpointView
ServiceEndpointView.description:
A port of a service. ``attribution`` states how the port was tied to the service:
``confirmed`` (socket owner observed), ``inferred`` (configuration / well-known port),
``unknown``. ``exposure`` derives from the bind address (``unknown`` also covers
public addresses).

ServiceInstanceItem.title: ServiceInstanceItem
ServiceInstanceItem.description: A process, container or Pod of a service (``v_service_instances_current``).

ServiceRef.title: ServiceRef
ServiceRef.description:
Reference from a SecurityEvent to the service that produced it.

Set only when the producing adapter can genuinely attribute the record (e.g.
sshd journald lines → the ssh service; container log → its Pod's workload).

ServicesSummary.title: ServicesSummary
ServicesSummary.description: Coverage of the services in scope (present services only; tombstones apart).

ServiceToken.description: API service token. Held only by the Next.js server; never sent to browsers.
